lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We left Sunrise Harbor, and now we're in a new town. Listen. Can you hear it? It's so noisy! Welcome to the Bustling Market! There are fruit shops, fish shops and bread shops. Today's sentence is: There are many shops. Say it with me. There are many shops. Great! For just one thing, say there is. There is a big fountain. For two or more, say there are. There are many shops. ひとつなら there is、ふたつ いじょうなら there are だよ。 Now, phonics. Look at these words. Boxes. Foxes. Buses. Glasses. When a word ends in x or s, we add e-s for two or more. Box, boxes. Bus, buses. Listen to the end. Iz, iz. x や s で おわる ことばは、es を つけて「イズ」と よむよ。 Here's a market tip. When you see something amazing, say, Wow, look at that! Let's say it. Wow, look at that! OK, grab a basket and stay together. Let's go shopping!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're at a fruit shop. Look at all the fruit! Kiko wants peaches. How can she ask? Today's sentence is: Do you have any peaches? Say it with me. Do you have any peaches? Great! When you ask a question, use any. Do you have any cherries? The answer can be, Yes, we have some. Or, Sorry, we don't have any. しつもんと「ない」ときは any、「ある」ときは some だよ。 Let's practice. Do you have any pears? Yes, we have some! Now, phonics. Peach. Peaches. Lunch. Lunches. Sandwich. Sandwiches. Bench. Benches. Words that end in c-h also get e-s. And the end sounds like iz. ch で おわる ことばも es を つけて「イズ」。 Here's a shopping tip. When the shopkeeper says hello, say hello back and smile. It makes shopping more fun. OK, let's find some fruit!

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! Mmm, can you smell that? It's the market bakery! Birimo is very hungry and wants some bread. Today's sentence is: Can I have some bread? Say it with me. Can I have some bread? Nice! Bread is special. We don't say one bread, two breads. We say some bread. パンや みず、ごはんは ひとつ ふたつと かぞえないよ。だから a ではなく some を つけるよ。 Water, rice, bread. Some water. Some rice. When the baker gives you the bread, she says, Here you go. Here you go means, this is for you. Now, phonics. Dish. Dishes. Brush. Brushes. Radish. Radishes. Bush. Bushes. Words that end in s-h get e-s, too. Iz, iz. Can you hear it? Great job! One more tip. Rolls are small pieces of bread, and we can count them. One roll, two rolls. Now, let's buy some bread for breakfast!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! It's hot today. Let's get something to drink. Look, there's a juice stand! Today's sentence is: A glass of orange juice, please. Say it with me. A glass of orange juice, please. Good! We can't count juice. One juice, two juices? No. We count the glasses. A glass of juice. Two glasses of juice. のみものは コップの かずで かぞえるよ。 Tea is hot, so we use a cup. A cup of tea. And for cake, we say a piece of cake. ケーキ ひときれ は a piece of cake。 Now, phonics. Tomato. Tomatoes. Potato. Potatoes. Hero. Heroes. When a word ends in o, sometimes we add e-s. And here, the end sounds like z. Tomatoes. Potatoes. Super! Here's a tip for drinks. If you want two, just say, two glasses, please. Easy! Now, which juice do you want? Orange, apple or tomato?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is game day! The inn kitchen gave us a shopping list. We have two teams. Which team can finish first? Today's sentence is: We need some eggs and two apples. Say it with me. We need some eggs and two apples. Great! Need means we must have it. We can count eggs and apples, so we say two apples, three eggs. But milk and bread? Some milk. Some bread. かぞえられる ものは かずを、かぞえられない ものは some を つけるよ。 To ask, say, Do we have any milk? No, we don't. Now, let's review our phonics. Boxes. Peaches. Dishes. Tomatoes. Glasses. You can read them all! And when you write your list, don't forget the e-s. Here's a team tip. Read the list out loud together. Then nobody forgets anything. Ready, set, go! Let's go shopping, team!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're visiting an old bookstore. Look at the tall shelves! There are so many books. Let's count by tens. Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, one hundred! Great job! Today's sentence is: It's a hundred yen. Say it with me. It's a hundred yen. Good! A hundred, or one hundred, is one, zero, zero. And ten hundreds is a thousand. 100 は a hundred、1000 は a thousand だよ。 To ask about a number, say, How many books are there? There are about a thousand! Now, phonics. Leaf. Leaves. Loaf. Loaves. Half. Halves. Shelf. Shelves. In some words that end in f, the f changes to v. Then we add e-s. f が v に かわるよ。 Wonderful! One tip. Fifteen and fifty sound similar. Fifteen is long at the end. Fif-teen. Fifty is short. Fif-ty. Listen carefully when people say prices!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're at a toy store. Haru finds a dancing robot. He loves it! But it's five thousand yen. Oh no! Today's sentence is: That's too expensive. Say it with me. That's too expensive. Good! Expensive means the price is high. Too expensive means it's more than you want to pay. たかすぎる、と いう ときは too expensive だよ。 Then you can ask, Do you have a cheaper one? Cheaper means it costs less. もっと やすいの、だよ。 Now, phonics. Knife. Knives. Wolf. Wolves. Scarf. Scarves. Calf. Calves. The f changes to v again. Knife ends in f-e, but it also becomes knives. Great! Here's a tip. When you find something good, say, I'll take it! That means, I want to buy this. Let's say it together. I'll take it! Now, let's look for a cheaper toy.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is a special day at the market. It's Market Day! On Market Day, kids take care of the shops. Today, you are the shopkeeper! When a customer buys something, say the price. That's three hundred and fifty yen, please. Then the customer gives you money. Five hundred yen. Now you give back the change. Today's sentence is: Here's your change. Thank you! Say it with me. Here's your change. Thank you! Excellent! Change is the money you give back. おつりの ことを change と いうよ。 At the end, say, Have a nice day! Now, phonics. Strawberries. Toys. Keys. Loaves. Strawberry has r before the y, so it's i-e-s. Toy and key have a vowel before the y, so just add s. y の まえが 母音なら s だけ だよ。 Wonderful! OK, shopkeepers. Put on your aprons and smile!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're at the dining hall in the market. Mmm, the soup smells so good! But what's in it? Today's sentence is: What's in the soup? Say it with me. What's in the soup? Good! To answer, say, There are carrots. There are onions. For things we can't count, like cheese, say, There is some cheese. かぞえられない ものは There is some だよ。 And if there's no fish, say, There isn't any fish. Now, a new kind of phonics! Look at this word. Knife. There's a k, but we don't say it. Knife. Knee. Knock. Know. The k is silent. It's a quiet letter. k は だまっている もじ。よまないよ。 Let's knock on the table. Knock, knock! Great! Here's a tip. If you're not sure, say, Maybe there are potatoes. Guessing is fun. Let's guess what's in the soup!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're in a cooking class. Put on your apron and wash your hands. Today we're making vegetable soup. Today's sentence is: First, cut the carrots. Say it with me. First, cut the carrots. Great! When we tell someone what to do, we start with an action word. Cut. Wash. Mix. Add. ひとに なにかを してもらう ときは、うごきの ことばから はじめるよ。 To show the order, say first, then next. First, cut the carrots. Next, wash the potatoes. And always, be careful with the knife! Now, phonics. Knot. Kneel. Knit. Knuckle. Remember, the k is silent. Kneel down. Knit a scarf. Tie a knot. Good job! Here's a cooking tip. Say the steps out loud, like a real chef. First, wash. Next, cut. It helps you remember them. OK, chefs. Let's start cooking!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome back to cooking class. Today we're making pancakes! Yum! First, put in two eggs and a cup of milk. Then add the flour. Today's sentence is: Mix it well. Then add some salt. Say it with me. Mix it well. Then add some salt. Good! Then means after that. It connects the steps. Then は「それから」。じゅんばんを つなぐ ことば だよ。 Mix. Add. Put in. These are cooking words. Now, phonics. Write. Wrap. Wrong. Wrist. Look at the first letter, w. But we don't say it! We start with the r sound. Write. Wrap. w は だまっている もじ だよ。 Shake your wrist. Mix, mix, mix! Great job! Here's a tip from Riko. Write the steps in your notebook, one step on each line. Then you can make pancakes at home with your family, too!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Our pancakes are ready! Look! They're golden and fluffy. Let's use our senses. Use your nose. It smells good! Use your mouth. It tastes sweet. Use your eyes. It looks delicious! Today's sentence is: It smells good! It tastes sweet. Say it with me. It smells good! It tastes sweet. Wonderful! After it, we add an s. Smells, tastes, looks. it の ときは s が つくよ（ワールド13 と おなじ）。 Other words: sweet, salty, sour, spicy, delicious. Now, phonics. Wrote. Wrapper. Wrinkle. Wreck. Again, the w is quiet. Wrote. Wrapper. Super! Here's a tip. When someone cooks for you, tell them how it tastes. It tastes great! Thank you! They'll be very happy. Let's practice once more. How does it smell? It smells good! How does it taste? It tastes sweet! Now, let's taste our pancakes!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is a special day. It's recipe presentation day! You bought food at the market and learned cooking words. Now, let's make a recipe together. Today's sentence is: Let's make fruit salad. Say it with me. Let's make fruit salad. Great! A good recipe has steps in order. First, wash the fruit. Next, cut it into small pieces. Then mix it with yogurt. Finally, enjoy! Finally means the last step. Finally は「さいごに」。 First, next, then, finally. Four steps! Now, let's review our phonics. Knife. Know. Knee. Write. Wrap. Remember the quiet letters. Excellent! Here's a presentation tip. Use your hands when you explain. Cut, cut. Mix, mix. People can understand you better. Now, it's your turn. lessons.teacherScript: Good evening, everyone! The food stalls are open tonight. There are lanterns everywhere. It's beautiful! Ms. Emma is the noodle cook. The noodles are delicious, but oh, my tummy is full! How can we say no nicely? Today's sentence is: No, thank you. I'm full. Say it with me. No, thank you. I'm full. Great! Saying no is OK. Just say thank you, too. ことわる ときも thank you を つければ ていねいだよ。 If you want a small amount, say, Yes, please. Just a little. Then add, It was delicious! The cook will smile. Now, phonics. Climb. Climber. Plumber. Thumbs. The b is quiet again. We say climb, not climb-buh. Good job! Here's a tip. When you say, Just a little, show it with your fingers. Like this. A little! Let's visit the food stalls!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're at a restaurant in the market. Riko can't eat eggs. Eggs make her sick, so she must be careful. Today's sentence is: I can't eat eggs. Say it with me. I can't eat eggs. Good! Some people can't eat eggs, milk or nuts. It's important to tell the waiter. たべられない ものは、おみせの ひとに はっきり つたえようね。 Then ask, Does this cake have eggs in it? The waiter checks. Yes, it does. Or, No, it doesn't. You can eat it. Now, new phonics! Phone. Photo. Phonics. Graph. P-h together makes the f sound. ph は f と おなじ おと だよ。 Phonics! That's what we're studying! Great job! Here's a tip. If you have a friend who can't eat something, remember it. Being kind to friends is important. Let's order some food!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're walking down the world food street. There are food stalls from many countries. But be careful. Some food is very spicy! Today's sentence is: Is it spicy? Say it with me. Is it spicy? Great! You can answer in three ways. A little. Yes, very. No, not at all. すこし、とても、ぜんぜん の 3つで こたえられるよ。 Let's learn taste words. Spicy, like chili. Sour, like lemons. Salty, like chips. Bitter, like dark chocolate. Make a sour face! Ha ha, great! Now, phonics. Elephant. Dolphin. Alphabet. Trophy. The p-h is in the middle of the word, but it still sounds like f. Elephant. Wonderful! Here's a tip. Before you eat something new, ask, Is it spicy? Then you won't get a big surprise. Let's go!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're visiting the world food corner. There's food from many countries here! Look. Pasta from Italy. Tacos from Mexico. Curry from India. Today's sentence is: People in Italy eat a lot of pasta. Say it with me. People in Italy eat a lot of pasta. Great! A lot of means many or much. たくさんの、は a lot of だよ。 People means more than one person, so we say eat, not eats. people は おおぜいなので eat に s は つけないよ。 Now, phonics. Twenty. Thirty. Forty. Fifty. The tens end in t-y. Be careful with forty. Four has a u, but forty doesn't! F-o-r-t-y. Good job! Here's a tip. When you talk about other countries, be curious and kind. Ask, What do people eat in your country? Let's travel around the world with food!

lessons.teacherScript: Good morning, everyone! What did you eat for breakfast today? Today we met a traveler at the market. In her country, many people eat bread and cheese for breakfast. In Japan, many people eat rice and miso soup. Today's sentence is: In Japan, many people eat rice for breakfast. Say it with me. In Japan, many people eat rice for breakfast. Great! Many people means a lot of people, but not everyone. おおくの ひと、ぜんいん では ないよ。 Then ask a friend, What do you usually eat for breakfast? I usually have toast and a glass of milk. Now, phonics. Sixty. Seventy. Eighty. Ninety. Eighty has only one t. Ninety keeps the e from nine. Let's spell ninety. N-i-n-e-t-y. Excellent! Here's a tip. When a friend answers, ask one more question. Oh, rice? What do you eat with it? Let's talk about breakfast!

phonics.tipJa: -teen（13〜19）は「ティーン」と のばして つよく、-ty（20, 30…）は みじかく。thirteen と thirty、fourteen と forty を ききわけよう。fourteen には u が あるよ！

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're in the market warehouse. There are boxes everywhere! Every food comes from somewhere. Today's sentence is: Bananas come from warm places. Say it with me. Bananas come from warm places. Great! Bananas means more than one, so we say come. For one food, we say comes. This cheese comes from a farm. ひとつなら comes、ふたつ いじょうなら come だよ。 To ask, say, Where does this cheese come from? It comes from a farm in the mountains. Now, phonics. Listen carefully. Thirteen. Thirty. Fourteen. Forty. Teen is long and strong. Thir-teen! T Y is short. Thir-ty. Can you hear the difference? -teen は のばして、-ty は みじかく。 Great job! Here's a tip. If you're not sure about a number, ask, Thirteen or thirty? Then the other person can say it again slowly. Let's count the boxes!

Today's sentence is: Vegetables are good for you. Say it with me. Vegetables are good for you. Great! Good for you means it helps your body. からだに いい、は good for you だよ。 Rice gives you energy. Fish makes you strong. Sweets are yummy, but don't eat too many sweets. Now, phonics. Hundred. Thousand. Fifteen. Fifty. Hundred is h-u-n-d-r-e-d. Thousand starts with t-h. Let's spell hundred together. H-u-n-d-r-e-d. Super! Here's a tip. A colorful lunch box is a healthy lunch box. Red tomatoes, green broccoli, yellow eggs. いろが たくさん だと えいようも たくさん。 What colors will you put in your lunch box? Let's plan our lunch boxes together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! It's the lunch box contest! Everyone made a lunch box. Now, let's show them to the judge. Today's sentence is: My lunch box has rice, eggs and broccoli. Say it with me. My lunch box has rice, eggs and broccoli. Great! When you list three things, put and before the last one. Rice, eggs and broccoli. 3つ ならべる ときは、さいごの まえに and。 Then talk about colors. The tomatoes are red, and the cucumbers are green. Finally, say, It's colorful and healthy. Please try it! Now, let's review the number spellings. Forty. Ninety. Fifteen. Hundred. Thousand. Can you spell forty? F-o-r-t-y. No u! Fantastic! Here's a presentation tip. Look at the judge and speak slowly. Show your lunch box with a big smile. Good luck, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is the market riddle contest! Let's make riddles about food. A good riddle has clues. A color, a shape, and when you eat it. lessons.teacherScript: Good evening, everyone! It's dinner time at the inn. Tonight, everyone tells a food story. A food story is about your favorite food and the people who make it. Today's sentence is: I love curry. My dad makes it on Sundays. Say it with me. I love curry. My dad makes it on Sundays. Great! My dad makes, with an s. Remember World 13? ワールド13 で ならった s が ここでも でるよ。 Add more. He puts in lots of vegetables. It's a little spicy, but I love it. But connects two different ideas. When your friend tells a story, use your conversation skills. Really? What kind? That's cool! Now, phonics review. Knock. Knit. Wrist. Wrong. Quiet k, quiet w. Good job! Here's a tip. Food stories are warm and happy. Share a memory with your food. Let's tell our stories!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're writing recipe cards. With a recipe card, you can cook the same food again and again. A recipe card has two parts. First, what you need. You need ten strawberries and some cream. Second, the steps. Today's sentence is: Wash the strawberries. Cut them in half. Say it with me. Wash the strawberries. Cut them in half. Great! Them means the strawberries. In half means into two pieces. them は「それら」、in half は「はんぶんに」。 Then, put them on a plate with some cream. Three steps! Now, phonics review. Comb. Climb. Photo. Elephant. The b is quiet, and p-h says f. Super! Here's a writing tip. Start each step with an action word, and write a number for each step. One, two, three. Let's write our recipe cards!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! This is our last day at the Bustling Market. Let's buy some souvenirs for our friends. Today we'll use all our shopping words. Today's sentence is: How much are these apples? Say it with me. How much are these apples? Great! They're eighty yen each. Each means for one. 1こ あたり、は each だよ。 Can I have five, please? Sure. That's four hundred yen. Here you go! If it's too expensive, say, That's too expensive. Do you have a cheaper one? And if you're full, No, thank you. I'm full. Now, phonics review. Eighty. Nineteen. Hundred. Thousand. Eighty has one t. Nineteen keeps the e. Wonderful! Oh, look! Something is shining behind the apple stand. Is it the golden apple from Birimo's map? Let's go and see!

lessons.teacherScript: Congratulations, everyone! This is the last lesson of World 14. ワールド14 さいごの レッスンだよ。 First, a speed challenge! Look! Stop! Come here! Go! Cut! Mix! Taste! Great! Now, it's the World 14 market show in the market square. Every team opens a shop and presents it. Today's sentences are: Welcome to our shop! Try our fruit salad! Say them with me. Welcome to our shop! Try our fruit salad! Wonderful! A good shop presentation has four parts. Welcome the customers. Recommend your food. Try our fruit salad! Explain how you make it. First, we cut the fruit. Then we mix it with honey. And tell the price. It's only a hundred yen! Now, the last phonics review. Boxes. Berries. Knife. Write. Phone. Fifty. Amazing! And look, the golden apple is opening. There's a new map inside! But first, your shop presentation. Smile big and speak loudly. You can do it!
